annotations.title: Check how much the birth time matters

description: Shows how sensitive a birth chart is to its birth time. It gives the exact clock window in which the rising sign held on the birth day and how far the stated time is from a change, then recalculates the chart for earlier and later birth times and lists what changes: the rising sign, the Navamsa rising sign, the Moon's nakshatra and pada, the Atmakaraka and the dates of the Vimshottari periods. Use it when someone is unsure of their exact birth time, asks whether a few minutes would change their chart, or wants to know which parts of their chart are safe to rely on.

birth_date.description: Date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD, for example 1990-01-15 for 15 January 1990. People write dates in different orders: day first in India and most countries, month first in the United States. Convert what the person wrote to YYYY-MM-DD yourself. If an all-number date could be read two ways, such as 05-06-1990, ask which number is the day before calling; never assume.

birth_place.description: City and country of birth, for example "Mumbai, India".

birth_time.description: Local clock time of birth at the birth place, 24-hour HH:MM, for example 10:30, or 16:26 for 4:26 PM. If the person gave an hour from 1 to 12 without AM or PM, ask which before calling. Ask the user if the time is unknown; do not guess it.

latitude.description: Optional. Latitude of the birth place in decimal degrees, north positive. Give it only together with longitude, when the user supplied coordinates or the place could not be found by name.

longitude.description: Optional. Longitude of the birth place in decimal degrees, east positive. Give it only together with latitude.

minutes.description: Optional. The largest birth-time error to test, in minutes either way. Defaults to 30.

name: check_birth_time_sensitivity
